Subject: Post-call: ACME integration & model routing (recap + next steps)

Tim — great chat earlier, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment and can prioritize the tech deep-dive.

High-level recap
- Goal: integrate Redwood inference into ACME's customer support pipeline for routing and reranking NLU responses while keeping 95th percentile latency under 250ms for short responses (<=128 tokens).
- Primary concerns you raised: auth & sandbox creds, routing by latency/cost, fallback chains for capacity degradations, and embedding/reranker performance for KB searches.

Key integration points we discussed
1) SDK & auth
   - Redwood SDK (Python/Node) for both streaming responses and embeddings. We can provide a private npm/pypi package or direct pip/npm install.
   - Auth options: API keys for sandbox; for prod we recommend service-account keys + mTLS or integration with your SSO/KMS (we can support short-lived tokens via our platform).
2) Model routing & policy config
   - Policy primitives: region routing, latency targets, cost buckets, fallback chains. Example: target low-latency route (quantized small model) for chat UX under 100ms; medium-quality route for business logic; high-quality route (bigger model) for policy/appeals.
   - Fallback chain: small -> medium -> cross-region medium (if local exhausted) -> hosted backup.
3) Structured output & tool calling
   - We support structured JSON outputs and tool calling (webhook invocation). We recommend deterministic schema + schema validation layer in Redwood to avoid regressions.
4) Embeddings & reranker
   - Use embeddings for candidate retrieval, then rerank with a cross-encoder. We recommend a two-stage pipeline: ANN (fast) -> reranker (small cross-encoder) -> final classification model.

Action items / next steps
- Marissa (me): send this recap + attach a short integration MVP doc and a model-routing policy template (attached).
- Dev: propose a sample SDK auth flow and recommended policy config for your use case; include an estimate of token costs vs latency trade-offs.
- ACME: confirm availability for a 60–90 minute technical deep-dive next week (we suggested Tue/Wed).

Attachments:
- integration_mvp.pdf (high-level MVP + timelines)
- model-routing-template.yaml (policy template you can copy into your config)

If that looks right, we'll schedule the technical session and Dev will bring a config proposal.

Thanks — Marissa

Hi Tim — quick technical response to the items you raised. Happy to go deeper in the technical session.

Auth / tokens
- We support OIDC for short-lived tokens and can issue tokens scoped to a service account. Integration pattern: ACME authenticates via Okta -> Redwood issues short-lived inference token (15m–1h) using an AD/SSO assertion. Keys can be stored/rotated in your KMS; we also support mTLS for private deployments.

SDK setup (quickstart)
- Python example: pip install redwood-sdk
  from redwood import Client
  client = Client(profile='acme-sandbox', token=os.environ['REDWOOD_TOKEN'])
  resp = client.generate(model='rw-medium-quant', input='...')

Model routing policy (conceptual template)
- policy_id: acme-support-v1
- routes: 
  - name: low-latency
    model: rw-small-quant
    max_latency_ms: 100
    cost_bucket: low
  - name: balanced
    model: rw-medium-quant
    max_latency_ms: 250
    cost_bucket: medium
  - name: high-quality
    model: rw-large-fp16
    max_latency_ms: 1000
    cost_bucket: high
- fallback_chain: [low-latency, balanced, cross-region-balanced, hosted-backup]
- region_priority: [us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1]

Notes on trade-offs
- Quantized small models are ~3–5x cheaper and 2–3x faster than fp16 large, but quality drop depends on prompt complexity. We recommend routing short informational responses to low-latency route and escalation/appeals to high-quality route.
- For reranker pipeline: use an ANN store (we can host or you can host with our affinity) that returns top-K, then run a cross-encoder reranker (rw-cross-small) before final scoring. This keeps p99 retrieval latency in the 50–120ms range for typical queries.

Index hosting recommendations
- Customer-managed: recommended if you need data locality and full control (you run Faiss/Annoy/Weaviate in your VPC).
- Redwood-managed: lower ops overhead; we provide encrypted indexes, region pinning, and autoscaling. For 2M docs we estimate a baseline vector store cost X (we'll provide a detailed estimate in the SoW).

Attachments: model-routing-template.yaml (policy template) attached. I'll prepare a short sample config we can test in the sandbox prior to the deep dive.

—Dev
